failure_summary.description: Misread the full parameter range and the stated anchor-count convention, introducing an unsupported exception and denominator adjustment.
Selected stronger or more elaborate claims—extra regularity, local-to-global implications, quantitative bounds, or estimate dependencies—without establishing them.
Treated a liminf condition, which permits subsequential blow-up, as equivalent to the required limsup condition.
Replaced the stated standard tableau class with a conjectured variant involving extra or omitted exclusion rules.

patch.reasoning: The batch repeatedly favored plausible but unproved refinements over the exact claim supported: altered domains or definitions, stronger regularity and quantitative conclusions, and relaxed logical conditions. Make option comparison more operational, especially for iff statements and added clauses. The existing skill already gives the exact Dyck-anchor and hypercube cautions, so these should not be duplicated.

edits.target: Before choosing an option, identify the exact definition or theorem the question is testing. Parse every displayed expression literally, then compare the options’ hypotheses, quantifiers, exponents, endpoint spaces, and requested level of detail. Do not invent a theorem, exceptional case, or stronger conclusion from analogy or from a plausible-sounding citation. If you cannot verify a stronger claim, select only what the stated result supports.
edits.content: Before choosing an option, identify the exact definition or theorem being tested and rewrite each choice as a literal claim, including its domain, quantifiers, and logical connectives. For an “if and only if” claim, check both directions; every added clause—such as a counterexample, numerical rate, uniformity in time, dependence of constants, or local-to-global implication—requires separate support. Parse limits exactly: limsup of a quantity being minus infinity means it eventually tends to minus infinity, while liminf being minus infinity may only assert a subsequence unless further structure is proved. A critical-looking parameter or plausible analogy does not establish a threshold or exception. Do not invent a theorem or citation; select only claims supported by a verified result or derivation.

For PDE regularity claims, keep the equation in its actual weak formulation and verify the hypotheses of the specific regularity theorem before upgrading the solution space. Formal integration by parts through rough coefficients is not automatic; for example, control of a matrix divergence is not control of all coefficient derivatives. Do not infer higher Sobolev regularity merely from ellipticity or VMO membership.

For named combinatorial classes such as tableau models, use the stated or standard definition exactly. Do not add, remove, or relocate an exclusion rule based on a guessed correspondence; a modified class is a distinct claim that must be established.
